record.question: A zero memory source generates two messages with probabilities 0.8 and 0.2. These are coded as 1 and 0.2. The code efficiency is
record.explanation: The printed Q31 on PDF page 4 (printed page 4) explicitly gives the codes as "1 and 0.2", so the defect is present in the source. This does not specify a valid binary code from which an average codeword length can be established; replacing "0.2" with "0" would give H = -0.8 log2(0.8) - 0.2 log2(0.2) = 0.7219 bits and efficiency 0.7219 for one-bit codewords, but that repair is unconfirmed. Hold pending clarification of the intended codewords.
